plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index concentration.
Add to QQQI to increase income focus.
Trim CRWD to 5% to reduce tech concentration.
Hold remaining cash buffer for capital preservation.
conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly return. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration risk, aiming for lower drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%) to reduce risk.
Trim SPY to 25% to address broad index concentration.
Initiate a new position in TSLA at 4% from the scanner.
Trim QQQI to 10% to balance income exposure.
Maintain a moderate cash buffer for flexibility.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% monthly return by blending index exposure with quality tech and some leverage. It aims for risk-first growth, reducing concentration and leverage while adding a new high-potential name.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL to 6%, SPAL to 6%) for amplified gains.
Add TSLA at 6% and CRWD at 10% from strong scanner setups.
Trim SMH to 5% to reduce exposure to underperforming semiconductors.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer to maximize invested capital.
Utilize wider but strict stops to manage increased risk.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% monthly return by concentrating capital in high-scoring setups and increasing leveraged ETF exposure. It accepts significantly higher potential drawdowns and the risk of rapid losses due to leverage and daily rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for stability.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index exposure.
Sell CRWD to eliminate high-beta single name risk.
Prioritize steady monthly distributions over growth potential.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly return through distributions, prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income. It shifts away from growth and leverage towards income-generating assets, though NAV can still decline in market downturns.
